scenarios.title: The Film You Hate
scenarios.text: You watch your own college film with the coaches, and it looks different now.

choices.label: Take notes on everything
choices.result: You take notes on every flaw the coaches point out. It's a long list, and it's useful.

choices.label: Fix one thing a week
choices.result: You pick one flaw a week and fix it. By midseason, the old film looks like someone else.

choices.label: Ask your college coach
choices.result: You call your college coach and talk through the film. He laughs and says he always knew.

scenarios.title: Your Parents in the Stands
scenarios.text: {parent} drives eleven hours to see you kick in person for the first time.

choices.label: Spend every minute together
choices.result: You spend every free minute with him. He doesn't stop smiling all weekend.

choices.label: Give him the full tour
choices.result: You give him the full tour: the locker room, the field, the coaches. He shakes {coach}'s hand twice.

choices.label: Keep your routine
choices.result: You keep your routine and see him after. He understands, and you wish you'd done more.

scenarios.title: The Sibling Who Wants to Visit
scenarios.text: {sibling} wants to spend his spring break at your apartment.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.result: You say yes and take him everywhere. He thinks you're the coolest person alive.

choices.label: Put him to work
choices.result: You let him come and help at your youth clinic. He's great with the kids.

choices.label: Say not this year
choices.result: You say this spring is too busy. He's disappointed.

scenarios.title: The College Teammates' Chat
scenarios.text: Your old college teammates' group chat wants inside stories from the league.

choices.label: Tell the funny ones
choices.result: You tell the funny stories and keep the private ones private. The chat loves you.

choices.label: Say nothing about the team
choices.result: You say you can't talk about the team. It's a little awkward, and it's right.

choices.label: Mute the chat
choices.result: You mute it for the season. You miss some jokes.

scenarios.title: The Old Girlfriend
scenarios.text: Someone from college messages you the week your first big headline runs.

choices.label: Meet for coffee
choices.result: You meet for coffee. It's warm and a little strange, and you're glad you went.

choices.label: Ask yourself why now
choices.result: You ask yourself why now, and don't answer. You keep it friendly from a distance.

choices.label: Leave it on read
choices.result: You leave it on read. It's simpler.

scenarios.title: Your First Bad Practice Week
scenarios.text: Five bad practices in a row, and the coaches have stopped saying 'next one'.

choices.label: Go back to basics with {coach}
choices.result: You ask {coach} to strip your routine back to basics. It's humbling, and it works.

choices.label: Kick until it's back
choices.result: You kick until the field lights come on, every night, until it's back.

choices.label: Talk to the holder
choices.result: You talk it through with {holder}, who has seen this before. It helps more than the kicking.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Car
scenarios.text: A veteran tosses you his keys and asks you to move his car, which costs more than your parents' house.

choices.label: Move it carefully
choices.result: You move it very carefully, and he notices. He starts calling you by your name.

choices.label: Ask what it cost
choices.result: You ask him what it cost and whether he'd do it again. His answer is long and honest.

choices.label: Hand the keys back
choices.result: You say you're not comfortable driving it. He laughs and moves it himself.

scenarios.title: Learning to Cook
scenarios.text: Your first apartment, and your diet is cereal and takeout.

choices.label: Learn to cook
choices.result: You learn five meals and cook them on rotation. Your energy in practice is better within a week.

choices.label: Cook with teammates
choices.result: You start a Sunday cooking night with two rookies. Everyone burns something; nobody cares.

choices.label: Meal service
choices.result: You sign up for a meal service. It's expensive, and you never think about food again.

scenarios.title: The Team Nutritionist
scenarios.text: The team nutritionist reviews what you eat and doesn't hide her reaction.

choices.label: Follow her plan
choices.result: You follow her plan to the letter. You feel better by week two.

choices.label: Ask for a performance plan
choices.result: You ask for a plan built for kicking power. It's strict and it works.

choices.label: Change one thing
choices.result: You change one thing: breakfast. It's a start.

scenarios.title: The Sleep Study
scenarios.text: The club puts every rookie through a sleep study, and your results are embarrassing.

choices.label: Fix your sleep
choices.result: You follow every recommendation: dark room, no phone, same bedtime. Your practices improve.

choices.label: Sleep more, simply
choices.result: You just go to bed an hour earlier. It helps.

choices.label: Compare with the rookies
choices.result: You compare results with the other rookies. Everyone's are bad, and you laugh about it for a week.

scenarios.title: The Team Psychologist
scenarios.text: The club's team psychologist offers you a standing Tuesday appointment.

choices.label: Take the Tuesday slot
choices.result: You take the slot. Some weeks you talk about kicking; most weeks you talk about everything else.

choices.label: Say you're fine
choices.result: You say you're fine. You are, mostly.

choices.label: Use it for routines
choices.result: You use the sessions to build a pre-kick routine. It's the best thing you do all year.

choices.label: Pick up where you left off
choices.result: You tell the psychologist what worked in college, and you skip the first month of getting to know each other.
choices.lock_text: having worked with a sports psychologist in college

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Doesn't Make It
scenarios.text: The rookie you came in with is released after his first season, and his locker is empty by noon.

choices.label: Help him pack
choices.result: You help him carry his things to the car. He thanks you for being the only one who came.

choices.label: Kick harder
choices.result: You kick harder that afternoon than you have all year.

choices.label: Call your agent
choices.result: You call your agent and ask what could have saved him. The answer is a list you take seriously.

scenarios.title: The Practice-Field Fan
scenarios.text: A kid watches every practice from behind the fence and holds up a sign with your name.

choices.label: Go say hello
choices.result: You walk over after practice and sign the sign. He's there every day after that, beaming.

choices.label: Get him on the field
choices.result: You ask the club to bring him onto the field for a practice. He kicks one ball and talks about it for years.

choices.label: Wave and keep going
choices.result: You wave and keep going. He waves back, every day.
